Importing NanoDrop Spectral Data

Source: vignettes/nanodrop-data-import.Rmd
nanodrop-data-import.Rmd

The export format

A NanoDrop One UV-Vis export holds one block per measurement: the sample name, a timestamp, a Wavelength (nm) header, some // calibration lines, and then wavelength/absorbance pairs:

6 1
5/14/2024 5:04 PM
Wavelength (nm) 10mm Absorbance
//WLCalib: Shift    0.22333
...
//QSpecEnd:
190.0   10.666
190.5   10.782
...

read_nanodrop() turns this into a long table with one row per measurement and wavelength.

Reading one file 

library(nanodRop)

path <- system.file("extdata", "nanodrop_example.tsv", package = "nanodRop")
spectra <- read_nanodrop(path)
head(spectra)
#>     samps waves    abs measurement         timestamp
#>    <char> <num>  <num>       <int>            <char>
#> 1:    6 1 190.0 10.666           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 2:    6 1 190.5 10.782           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 3:    6 1 191.0 10.853           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 4:    6 1 191.5 10.877           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 5:    6 1 192.0 10.866           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM
#> 6:    6 1 192.5 11.105           1 5/14/2024 5:04 PM

The columns are:

  • samps: sample name as typed on the instrument
  • waves: wavelength (nm)
  • abs: absorbance
  • measurement: position of the block in the file. If you measure the same sample twice, the two measurements stay separate.
  • timestamp: timestamp line as written by the instrument

Use min_wv and max_wv to keep part of the spectrum:

visible <- read_nanodrop(path, min_wv = 400, max_wv = 700)
range(visible$waves)
#> [1] 400 700

Re-measured samples

Some labs mark a re-measurement by adding a suffix to the sample name, for example "A" followed later by "Ae". Set remeasure_suffix to have the re-measurement replace the original:

read_nanodrop(path, remeasure_suffix = "e")

Only names whose original is also in the file are affected. A sample called "Rinse" stays "Rinse" unless there is also a sample called "Rins".

Reading a folder of exports

read_nanodrop_dir() reads every .tsv file in a folder and adds a file column:

folder <- system.file("extdata", package = "nanodRop")
all_spectra <- read_nanodrop_dir(folder)
unique(all_spectra$file)
#> [1] "nanodrop_example.tsv"

Plotting 

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(spectra, aes(waves, abs, colour = samps, group = measurement)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Wavelength (nm)", y = "Absorbance", colour = "Sample") +
  theme_minimal()
